prs.body:
## Current revision — November 27

This revises the existing ownership proposal on current develop, preserves its original commits, and keeps the earlier **HOLD** evidence below. The added optimization reuses the owned **Uint16 expression-ID column** at the immediate parser-worker transfer boundary. Generic copy-helper callers retain independent snapshots. The original retained-record key-arena safeguard is carried forward.

The additional expression column removes **30,452,656 bytes of cumulative allocations across the three current corpora**. Key-arena/key-length reuse is prior #820 work; the entire combined reduction is not a new discovery.

### Complete current-corpus proof

| Dictionary | Rows | Total cumulative buffers removed | Expression-column portion |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| JMdict | 528,299 | 10,434,868 B | **2,113,196 B** |
| Jitendex | 436,555 | 11,477,248 B | **1,746,220 B** |
| VNDB | 6,648,310 | 229,184,826 B | **26,593,240 B** |
| Total | 7,613,164 | 251,096,942 B | **30,452,656 B** |

These are actual unique emitted backing-buffer counts under the existing three-worker grouping, summed over the import. They are **not peak memory, bytes copied over IPC, or import-time savings**. The expression portion is the exact arithmetic `4 × whole-index rows`; it is not a separately timed key-only control.

The actual parser-worker handler, compressed-source inflate/CRC, real transfer list and structured-clone detachment pass full content/key/numeric/metadata/dedup/media/index parity under existing 2-, 3- and 5-worker groupings: **616 groups / 22,839,492 row comparisons**. Previous owned results survive later native heap reuse. The two-worker JMdict replay also covers the unchanged segmented path. Execution is sequential and does not model browser scheduling.

- Baseline: `9e10d3b3fcf66d344ab31bc42c9b522fa5215da2`.
- Current revision: `f65f4ef97ebf2f37a5b1b79ca7733d7b362ec963`; tree `9c34079709e7b8f6cae6b61c9ef537bb965ebcee`.
- [Exact source, raw evidence, failed attempts and reproduction index](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/tree/f65f4ef97ebf2f37a5b1b79ca7733d7b362ec963/builds/perf/import-owned-columns-83b3-evidence).
- [Experiment handoff](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/blob/f65f4ef97ebf2f37a5b1b79ca7733d7b362ec963/dev/perf/import-experiments-20260914.md).

### Validation and browser qualification

**22 focused tests, scoped strict TypeScript, scoped repository ESLint, and source whitespace checks pass.** [Static web acceptance](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/46103918233) also passed on the exact product tree: main/test/web types, 78 focused tests, and 24 no-extension browser scenarios covering full JMdict/Jitendex imports, restart, cancellation/recovery and offline lookup. [Actionlint](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/46103918146) and dependency review pass. [Normal CI](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/46103918118) is **fully passing: all 15 enabled gates**, including all four type projects, lint, both Chromium and Firefox full-extension E2E, the pinned native rebuild, the options suite, and the complete unit suite: **670 files / 15,152 tests passed, 47 existing skips**. Four conditional lanes were skipped, not counted as passes. The [registered performance qualification](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/46103918280) has finished all four cells and all 136 planned imports. Its final status is failure solely because VNDB candidate memory observation B1 did not meet the fixed sampling-coverage limit; the detailed HOLD decision is below. The native WASM is unchanged. The final corpus runner passed independent review; its earlier eager-diagnostic serialization failure and other failed attempts remain preserved and are excluded from performance interpretation.

The registered hosted study used two independent, opposite-order JMdict cells with **12 candidate pairs each**, plus six-pair Jitendex and VNDB cells. Each retains identical-code controls, fresh profiles, post-UI completion, persisted readback/restart checks, separate exhaustive media verification, and separate audited memory observations. Source/package guards permit exactly the parser, parser-worker and retained-record-store changes. No worker, grouping, compression, cache or dictionary policy is changed. A separate baseline JMdict trace is diagnostic only.

### Completed browser study: HOLD

The [complete raw evidence and independent readbacks for all four cells](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/tree/7a48cd9dea074d4d92f3456b4911c9e2aacdd744/builds/perf/import-owned-columns-83b3-hosted) are durably preserved, including every control, tail and raw memory scan. Only the original product ZIP payloads are excluded from the compact derivative archives; their verified complete inventories and digests remain. All non-package observations are retained.

Independent readback verifies every complete timing schedule, raw browser monotonic endpoint, exact source/package/fixture binding, all 2/3/5 component replay policies, post-UI readback/restart and exhaustive-media gate. The first three cells also pass separate memory qualification. VNDB's sole failed gate is memory coverage, described below. These results belong to current head `f65f4ef97ebf2f37a5b1b79ca7733d7b362ec963`; earlier historical cohorts remain separate.

Negative changes are faster. Each row is one host. Equal work compares summed matched durations. Identical-code C/A controls remain separate, without subtraction or host pooling.

| Cell | Candidate B/A median | Candidate equal work | Faster pairs | Identical C/A median | Identical C/A equal work |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| JMdict, initial AB | +0.2584% | +0.4499% | 6/12 | +1.0747% | +0.2374% |
| JMdict, initial BA | +0.0487% | +2.2435% | 6/12 | +1.2052% | +0.1371% |
| Jitendex, initial AB | +2.5895% | +2.0372% | 1/6 | −0.7962% | −0.7864% |
| VNDB, initial AB | −1.6899% | −1.6389% | 5/6 | +1.7890% | +1.7943% |

**Neither independent JMdict host demonstrates a latency improvement.** Its BA host retains two slow candidate pairs (+11.2233% and +10.1601%). Jitendex leans slower and is order-sensitive: its AB and BA strata medians are +0.4019% and +3.9555%. VNDB's favorable timing median remains unqualified under the complete protocol, and its worst candidate pair (+2.3119%) is retained.

All four descriptive 95% intervals include zero: JMdict AB [−1.164%, +2.206%], JMdict BA [−1.477%, +6.120%], Jitendex [−0.618%, +4.187%], and VNDB [−4.058%, +0.871%]. No optional unchanged-source repetition or tail exclusion was performed.

Each separate memory cell contains only two adjacent pairs. The figures describe maxima among covered Chromium process-tree samples, including startup/readback/restart; they are not exact import peaks.

| Cell | Sampled private-memory median change | Sampled PSS median change | Qualification |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| JMdict AB | +0.0416% | +0.1861% | Passed |
| JMdict BA | +0.3660% | +0.3497% | Passed |
| Jitendex AB | −2.4384% | −1.9647% | Passed |
| VNDB AB | Withheld | Withheld | B1 coverage failed |

**VNDB failure:** candidate memory B1 has a **253.533022 ms** maximum covered import-sampling gap, above the unchanged **250 ms** limit. Its private/PSS maxima correctly remain null; pair 1 and the aggregate memory screen remain unqualified. All four memory imports exited 0 and `semantic-failures.json` is empty. This is insufficient measurement coverage, not a measured memory regression or import failure. The one qualified pair 2 is retained but cannot replace pair 1. The limit was not relaxed, and no run was replaced. A [separate independent raw-scan review](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/blob/7a48cd9dea074d4d92f3456b4911c9e2aacdd744/builds/perf/import-owned-columns-83b3-analysis-source/vndb-memory-independent-review.json) confirms the exact gap.

The small Jitendex sampled-memory reduction is descriptive. JMdict does not show a memory reduction here. The deterministic cumulative allocation saving remains the concrete mechanism result.

### Further investigation and preserved evidence

[The complete follow-up evidence bundle](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/blob/bc26b191ba38d3b5cfd90d4c88584883720d267c/builds/perf/import-owned-columns-83b3-followup/README.md) preserves all 153 independently verified files: fixed request-batching and aligned-checksum cohorts, exact inputs, controls, failures, corrected canonical-sink profiles, complete native-symbol proof, and the compressed-input JMdict diagnostic. Neither additional runtime experiment established a useful gain. The evidence is on a separate branch; this PR's runtime head and the acquired study remain unchanged. The historical executor-interruption snapshot is retained separately. The completed [baseline browser trace readback and additive sampling correction](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/tree/cf43df9f197b729085950dc9f2f7b3ee7a773e35/builds/perf/20261128-browser-jmdict-profile-83b3) preserve the full raw trace and correct the initial sampling-gap interpretation without modifying earlier raw archives. Separately, [#830](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/pull/830) now contains a current-source 17 ms direct-registration result and its own prospective browser qualification; it is not pooled with this ownership study.

**Status remains draft/HOLD.** The allocation reduction is concrete; the completed study does not establish a qualified complete-browser speed or exact peak-memory benefit. Historical results below belong to their original source and fixtures and will not be pooled with the current study.

<details>
<summary>Historical November 23 proposal and completed HOLD evidence — preserved unchanged</summary>

## Problem

Native whole-chunk lookup indexes already contain an owned UTF-8 key arena and key-length table. The parser result copies both again into its key plan before transfer, adding work and another backing allocation.

## Change

When the native producer owns the complete sidecar and row byte lists are omitted, let its key plan refer to those exact owned subviews. A private WeakMap witnesses the producer and descriptor identities. Replaced descriptors fall back to ordinary copying; in-place edits stay visible to the current validation path. Explicit row-byte-list callers keep their existing aliases and copying behavior. Segmented and arbitrary split plans retain their existing contracts.

Retained record caches detach one tightly sized key arena when keeping a subview would otherwise pin the whole prepared sidecar. Normal OPFS imports discard these materialized records and keep the copy reduction. No grouping, concurrency, compression, or persisted format changes.

## Correctness and work reduction

- Complete stable row/content/media/key-plan/index outputs match baseline for all 526,942 JMdict, 435,448 Jitendex and 6,648,310 VNDB rows.
- Summed duplicate copied bytes removed in the serial corpus partitions: **8,301,780 JMdict; 9,706,463 Jitendex; 202,591,586 VNDB**. These are copy/allocation-volume reductions, not peak-memory or elapsed-time claims. Partitions have production-shaped group counts; exact bank membership was not independently matched to the browser planner.
- 234 parser/boundary and 195 record-store tests passed. Ownership coverage includes detached/transferred buffers, source reuse, descriptor replacement, in-place edits, explicit byte lists and retained-cache backing-buffer size/mutation independence.
- Main types, scoped lint and all-target build dry runs passed. The local complete test-type process was killed with exit 137 and no diagnostics; that original failure remains retained. [Hosted full CI 45122913657 passed](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/45122913657), including the complete test-type gate, unit suites, pinned build, and Chromium/Firefox extension E2E. Optional workflow lanes were skipped, not represented as passes.
- Native WASM is unchanged.

## Performance decision: HOLD

Keep draft. The completed timing campaign does not establish a repeatable material complete-import gain. Four independent memory cells support small descriptive sampled-memory reductions; both JMdict memory cells remain unqualified. No all-corpus memory qualification or exact browser peak-memory claim is made.

### Complete-browser timing

[Run 45123053286](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/45123053286) completed all six cells and **252 fresh-profile imports**: six excluded warmups, twelve adjacent alternating candidate/parent pairs and six interleaved same-code C/A pairs per cell, with independent reversed-order replication. Independent source/package, fixture/work, raw operation-clock and statistical checks pass. Timing used Node 22.22.0 / Chromium 153.0.8010.12, identical production defaults and OPFS storage through the post-UI import-complete event. Twelve source-derived persisted probes and restart verification passed for every import.

Entries are **forward / reverse**; negative is faster. Equal work compares summed paired durations within one cell. No hosts are pooled and no control effects are subtracted.

| Dictionary | B/A median, F / R | B/A equal work, F / R | C/A median, F / R | C/A equal work, F / R |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| JMdict | −0.50% / +0.53% | +0.11% / +0.93% | −0.37% / +1.09% | −0.87% / +1.07% |
| Jitendex | +0.37% / +1.73% | +0.22% / +1.60% | −0.53% / +0.66% | −4.26% / +0.99% |
| VNDB | −1.22% / −0.95% | +0.67% / −1.03% | −0.63% / +0.95% | −0.52% / +0.72% |

VNDB's result-copy equal-work counters decrease 7.24% / 6.21%, consistent with the intended mechanism. Its forward timing cohort retains two +12.05% / +13.07% slower pairs, yielding +0.67% equal work despite a favorable median interval. Reverse's median interval includes zero. JMdict and Jitendex are slower on equal work in both directions. Copy counters are overlapping worker-duration sums, not wall-time savings. Frozen timing study source: `9941723a323c76e8d73a16880e658fa243f17187`.

### Separate process-tree memory diagnostics

[Run 45124025705](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/45124025705) completed all 24 browser imports. Four complete cells qualified for memory comparisons; each cell contains two adjacent pairs. The table preserves each independent job and does not pool memory estimates across hosts.

| Dictionary | ABBA sampled PSS / private median | BAAB sampled PSS / private median |
|---|---:|---:|
| JMdict | Unqualified — coverage failure | Unqualified — coverage failure |
| Jitendex | −0.54% / −0.55% | −4.79% / −5.82% |
| VNDB | −2.29% / −2.75% | −2.52% / −2.88% |

Both JMdict cells contain one unreadable stable two-thread zombie leader, outside the frozen single-thread-zombie exemption. Their maxima and comparisons remain withheld, with failure receipts retained and no salvaged scans or retries. These are measurement-coverage failures, not import failures or measured regressions.

These values are maxima of covered, discovered Chromium process-tree samples during startup, import, readback and restart. They are not exact import peaks or settled-memory measurements; scans are non-atomic and may miss short-lived/reparented processes. Observer-run elapsed times are not authoritative speed evidence. Frozen memory study source: `a9a90967f1dfc9c9c68d06ae5ad4ad1e999f67b2`; unchanged observer SHA-256: `ca6c0f7761062761697a810d4bd0007ff0257bbce69099df45657ffdb7ee8f10`.

**HOLD under the repository acceptance rule:** the copy/memory evidence is scoped and useful, but a material replicated complete-import benefit and complete memory qualification are absent. All raw observations, slow tails, full-data oracle receipts and local/measurement failures remain in #814. Sampled browser probes do not replace exhaustive persisted-database equality.

Baseline: `5e1f8c12f7ff798ba407323aff675cb23b22af02`. Runtime: `8fe5926cec1396a05ed4ea52be751e48784329b7`. Exact published tree: `df4e570212e6ef8a60f12f578b57c6d04455faa3`.

</details>

prs.title: Move owned lookup envelopes to the import I/O worker
prs.body:
## Problem

The locked VNDB diagnostic recorded 192 contiguous lookup envelopes totaling 401,899,752 bytes on the storage owner. [Three diagnostic imports](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/pull/868) attributed a median 413.9 ms to this synchronous work. It hashes and copies payloads before transferring the finished envelopes to the existing import I/O worker.

## Changes

Keep privately owned envelopes as header, payload, and record-field buffers. Validate and atomically transfer their ownership before any asynchronous handoff, then compute checksums inside the existing ordered I/O worker queue and write the parts through its bounded coalescer.

Ownership receipts originate at the production parser-worker receiver and fresh store field encoder. Replaced descriptors, shared/partial/resizable buffers, duplicate buffers, and retained key, content, or media aliases retain the eager snapshot path. Native segmented key-plan aliases remain alive.

The existing worker eligibility threshold, byte admission budget, logical envelope counts, sticky failures, flush order, and persistent format remain unchanged. No new worker or retained dictionary cache is introduced.

## Verification

- 92 focused tests pass, including actual parser and I/O workers, materialized and persisted-only records, native segmentation, malformed-result settlement, short writes, blocked periodic flushes, failure precedence, and rollback.
- Main and test TypeScript, changed-file ESLint, and all-target dry build pass.
- Four exact real VNDB source groups passed through the production worker receiver and public record append: 158,310 rows, all four envelopes and 9,325,848 bytes adopted, zero eager fallbacks. Complete output bytes match both the eager implementation and the previously captured baseline hashes; key plans remain intact.
- Runtime JavaScript grows by 16,614 uncompressed bytes across seven files, including two new modules. No WASM, dependency, or persistent-format changes.

## Qualification

Full hosted [CI](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/45466987463) passed on exact candidate `1a04064bcc33565537c47f8047dacd03b3e89b24`: full unit/options suites, all four TypeScript projects, lint, pinned native rebuild, release build, Chromium/Firefox extension E2E, Chromium Anki matrix, and restart/interruption recovery.

The completed standalone [timing campaign #878](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/pull/878) retained all 132 scheduled observations, including 108 timed imports, across two independent hosts for each dictionary. Both VNDB hosts improved their median but **failed the predeclared target requirement of at least 5% versus both identical-code controls on each host**:

| VNDB host | Median paired B/A change | Median paired B/C change | Faster pairs versus A / C |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 0 | −2.507084% | −3.106240% | 6/6 / 6/6 |
| 1 | −2.725951% | −4.668217% | 5/6 / 4/6 |

All four JMdict and Jitendex timing cells passed the non-target regression screen. The separate [memory campaign #879](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/pull/879) retained all 24 observations and 2,696 raw scans. Twenty observation windows qualified; four failed coverage. One fully covered Jitendex pair exceeded the private-memory limit (+12.222016380%). JMdict host 2 and VNDB host 1 instead failed scan coverage, with invalid maxima and pairs kept null. All semantic and exhaustive-media checks passed. These observations do not establish the cause of the memory variation.

**This standalone candidate did not qualify for promotion and remains draft.** All observations, archive identities, failures, and unchanged decision rules are preserved in the completed measurement PRs. No selective rerun or threshold change was made.

### Completed combined evaluation

[Campaign #882](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/pull/882) separately measured the unchanged composition of this PR and the independently developed [single-image projector #875](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/pull/875). Median paired VNDB reductions ranged from 3.849969% to 5.992965% across the two hosts and two controls. One host missed the frozen 5% requirement, so the two-host timing gate failed. All four JMdict/Jitendex regression screens passed.

All 24 combined memory observations were acquired. Four baseline windows failed scan coverage, preventing memory qualification; no measured memory threshold breach occurred in the final composition. Source and semantic validation passed. These combined results do not establish this change's incremental benefit over #875 alone.

The source remains draft. No candidate, threshold or workload changed after freezing, and no failed observation was replaced. The published standalone tree remains `11f797eb59be5c92a4b3fbb6549949cab9be2a28`; the complete combined source identities and observations follow.

prs.title: perf(import): overlap bounded owned JMdict content preparation
prs.body:
## Why this is worth reviewing

JMdict currently finishes the ordered content/record sink for one owned group before the next group can prepare its content. Existing reserved content offsets make a narrower dependency possible: after the first group's metadata is published, the next immutable group can prepare deduplication/compression while the first group finishes persistence.

A completed, source-bound scheduling prototype showed a repeatable compression-component gain with the actual **1 MiB database block target**. This draft implements that mechanism with bounded ownership and failure handling. **HOLD: no whole-import speedup or browser-memory pass has been established.**

## What changes

- Admit at most two eligible append owners. The successor starts content preparation after predecessor metadata publication; its metadata and record writes still wait for predecessor completion.
- Preserve immutable parser ownership through full completion. Producer lead, owned-byte accounting, source release, progress, and metrics retire at completion.
- Latch failure/cancellation, join every started operation, and unwind successor metadata before predecessor rollback. Legacy completion-only appends use the same queue.
- Claim finalization ownership before draining active appends, preserving the existing synchronous behavior when no owner is pending.
- Continue physical worker assignment across adjacent shared-span compression batches. All four workers were already active in the corrected workload; this balances partial worker rounds.
- Account overlapping sink wall intervals by their union when deriving parser wall time; retain per-consumer work sums.

Cross-group preparation requires complete immutable owned shared content, complete native dedup metadata, and the existing JMdict compression path. The worker cursor applies to all shared-span batches, so cross-corpus timing checks remain required even where the sink stays serial. Borrowed, private, partial, unwitnessed, media, and otherwise ineligible chunks keep completion-ordered sink behavior. Codec settings, block geometry, worker counts, producer budgets, and stored formats stay fixed.

The diff contains **seven runtime files, six focused test files, and the required copyright-header registration**. It contains no experiment harness or unrelated optimization.

## Completed gain evidence and its scope

The corrected replay uses frozen baseline `9e10d3b3fcf66d344ab31bc42c9b522fa5215da2`, exact native-parser/dedup spans for **528,299 JMdict rows**, 12 groups, 100,300,626 input bytes, and **103 blocks**. It runs the shipped codec and dictionary on four real Node workers. Twelve rounds balance all six A/B/C orders twice; all 36 observations are retained.

| Comparison | Paired median change | Equal-work change | Faster pairs |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Prototype B / serial A | **−13.0747 ms / −16.5153%** | −17.2931% | 12/12 |
| Prototype B / identical serial C | **−10.6451 ms / −12.9197%** | −15.2888% | 11/12 |
| Identical C / A | −1.0119 ms / −1.1922% | −2.3661% | 7/12 |

Elapsed arm medians are A 78.6873 ms, B 67.5730 ms, and C 78.0943 ms. Their difference is a different statistic from the paired median change.

**This is a scheduling prototype, not a timing run of this PR's runtime.** B rotates the baseline pool's worker array and permits two pending codec groups. The committed cursor uses the same successful physical-worker sequence, but production's metadata-publication gate can make its useful overlap window narrower. Parsing, dedup, records, OPFS, browser transport, and UI are excluded. All arms also drift downward during the cohort; balanced orders and the identical control reduce simple order bias but do not establish a stable production magnitude.

All 36 timed observations have identical per-block compressed hashes and output bytes. One separate verification-only run decodes all 103 blocks and matches every input block; this does not claim 36 separate decode passes.

A separate 100-observation five-arm ablation favors the combined mechanism, but its identical-control drift makes the magnitude inconclusive. Rotation alone is not established as a worthwhile optimization. The earlier 4 MiB/31-block screen is superseded and is not the basis for this draft.

Immutable evidence:

- [All 36 observations, paired arithmetic, exact source and fixture bindings](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/blob/a1f7c234db525d960b38a90f1930b7354f1cb18e/builds/perf/import-overlap-20261128-da6c4/corrected-codec-review-receipt.json).
- [Exact corrected replay source](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/blob/a1f7c234db525d960b38a90f1930b7354f1cb18e/builds/perf/import-overlap-20261128-da6c4/corrected-codec-replay.mjs). Its inherited warmup comment about an idle fourth worker applies to the superseded 4 MiB screen; all four are active at 1 MiB.
- [Raw evidence archive and member hashes](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/blob/a1f7c234db525d960b38a90f1930b7354f1cb18e/builds/perf/import-overlap-20261128-da6c4/components-v1-index.json), including complete timings, ablation, failed attempts, and DB/store parity receipts.
- [Full experiment handoff and later validation history](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/blob/a1f7c234db525d960b38a90f1930b7354f1cb18e/dev/perf/import-experiments-20260914.md).

## Correctness and validation provenance

The full DB/store replay is bound to the **original implementation `a20453bc`**, not the later repaired runtime. It covers all 528,299 rows, exact metadata/dedup results, all 103 compressed blocks, persisted content/record hashes, and 36 source-derived reopened probes per arm. Only validated random generation IDs are masked. A forced-response gate proves successor compression starts before predecessor completion. SQLite setup/journaling/COMMIT and the browser producer are outside that replay.

The current runtime `5048ba3e` repairs three cleanup/finalization regressions exposed by existing tests, fixes overlapping diagnostic clocks, and resolves the original lint diagnostics. It has:

- **146 passing tests across seven focused/cleanup suites**, including all 66 existing cleanup tests with their assertions unchanged.
- **All seven build targets passing**.
- Passing exact-config lint for the three repaired test files and a clean diff check.

Complete current lint, all type projects, the full unit suite, and browser qualification remain pending. Local whole-suite/type attempts exited 137 or exhausted their configured heaps; they are incomplete, not passes. Earlier main/scoped type passes belong to the earlier runtime and are not relabeled as current-head passes.

This clean branch's entire **`ext/` tree, `test/` tree, and ESLint configuration exactly match `5048ba3e8a65fc41b9ae898c47b54d5731cd759e`**. Research-only files are excluded. Normal PR checks run unchanged.

## Gates before promotion

[The frozen current-runtime qualification](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/46108795917) first requires full lint, main/test types, unit tests, and builds. It then covers JMdict, Jitendex, and VNDB in independent AB/BA cells, each with 12 timing pairs, four warmups, interleaved identical-code controls, exhaustive media checks, and separate process-tree memory observations. Existing PSS/private bounds remain +5% paired median and +10% per pair, with the prospective sampling-coverage checks intact.

Retaining two owned source groups increases the live source window; the earlier component's sampled RSS is not a peak or browser-memory qualification. Cancellation/finalization ordering and this retained-owner memory cost are the main review risks. This draft stays held until current validation and browser correctness, performance, and memory evidence justify promotion.

This differs from #874's within-one-private-batch experiment and #955's borrowed-source release work. It also does not include the separate FIFO-dispatch or VNDB raw-alias experiments.

+import {hashTermLookupKeyBytes, splitPersistedTermLookupIndex} from './term-lookup-index.js'
+
+/** @typedef {{header: Uint8Array, payload: Uint8Array, recordFields: Uint8Array, byteLength: number}} DeferredImportIndexChunk */
+/** @typedef {Uint8Array|DeferredImportIndexChunk} ImportIndexChunk */
+
+/**
+ * Preserve each logical chunk's exact on-disk byte sequence without allocating
+ * its concatenated envelope. The owner already validated and snapshotted the
+ * authoritative fields. Hash the same immutable bytes that the writer uses.
+ * @param {ImportIndexChunk[]} chunks
+ * @returns {Uint8Array[]}
+ * @throws {Error} If the private chunk framing is inconsistent.
+ */
+export function prepareImportIndexChunkParts(chunks) {
+    /** @type {Uint8Array[]} */
+    const parts = []
+    for (const chunk of chunks) {
+        if (chunk instanceof Uint8Array) {
+            parts.push(chunk)
+            continue
+        }
+        const {header, payload, recordFields, byteLength} = chunk
+        if (
+            !(header instanceof Uint8Array) || header.byteLength !== 40 ||
+            !(payload instanceof Uint8Array) || !(recordFields instanceof Uint8Array) ||
+            byteLength !== header.byteLength + payload.byteLength + recordFields.byteLength
+        ) { throw new TypeError('Invalid import index chunk parts') }
+        const view = new DataView(header.buffer, header.byteOffset, header.byteLength)
+        const {base, derived} = splitPersistedTermLookupIndex(payload)
+        if (view.getUint32(16, true) !== payload.byteLength || view.getUint32(20, true) !== base.byteLength) {
+            throw new Error('Invalid import index chunk lengths')
+        }
+        view.setUint32(24, hashTermLookupKeyBytes(base), true)
+        view.setUint32(28, hashTermLookupKeyBytes(derived), true)
+        view.setUint32(32, hashTermLookupKeyBytes(recordFields), true)
+        parts.push(header, payload, recordFields)
+    }
+    return parts
+}
